questions.stem: What is essential for seeing or visibility along with the eyes?
questions.solution: Light is essential for seeing or visibility along with the eyes. Without light, the eyes cannot detect objects because there is no illumination to reflect off surfaces. Other options like air, sound, and heat do not play a direct role in the process of visual perception.

hi.solution: आंखों के साथ दृश्यता या दृष्टि के लिए प्रकाश आवश्यक होता है। प्रकाश के बिना, आंखें वस्तुओं को नहीं देख सकतीं क्योंकि सतहों पर प्रकाश के परावर्तन के बिना कोई उजाला नहीं होता। अन्य विकल्प जैसे हवा, ध्वनि और ऊष्मा दृष्टि अपसारण की प्रक्रिया में सीधा भूमिका नहीं निभाते।

questions.stem: Which type of reflection occurs when light rays fall on a smooth surface like a plane mirror?
questions.solution: Regular reflection occurs when light rays hit a smooth surface and reflect in a parallel manner, maintaining their direction. Irregular reflection happens on rough surfaces where light scatters in different directions. Scattering refers to light spreading out in multiple directions, not a type of reflection. Absorption is when light is taken in by a material, not reflected.

hi.stem: किस प्रकार के परावर्तन की स्थिति में प्रकाश की किरणें एक चिकनी सतह जैसे समतल दर्पण पर गिरती हैं?
hi.solution: जब प्रकाश की किरणें एक चिकनी सतह पर गिरती हैं और समांतर रूप से परावर्तित होती हैं, तो नियमित परावर्तन होता है, जो अपनी दिशा बनाए रखती है। कच्ची सतहों पर अनियमित परावर्तन होता है जहां प्रकाश विभिन्न दिशाओं में बिखर जाता है। बिखराव का अर्थ है प्रकाश का विभिन्न दिशाओं में फैल जाना, जो परावर्तन का एक प्रकार नहीं है। अवशोषण तब होता है जब कोई पदार्थ प्रकाश को अवशोषित कर लेता है, न कि परावर्तित करता है।

questions.stem: What happens to light when it moves through a tiny hole in a cardboard box?
choices: It spreads out in all directions
It forms an inverted image on the screen
questions.solution: When light moves through a tiny hole in a cardboard box, it forms an inverted image on the screen because the light rays from the top of an object pass through the hole and hit the bottom of the screen, while rays from the bottom pass through and hit the top. This occurs due to the straight-line travel of light, creating an inverted image. The other options are incorrect because light does not spread out in all directions like a wave, nor does it bend or disappear completely.

questions.stem: If the angle of incidence is 30°, what is the angle of reflection?
questions.solution: The law of reflection states that the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection. Therefore, if the angle of incidence is 30°, the angle of reflection must also be 30°. The other options do not match this fundamental principle of reflection. 0° and 90° are not consistent with the relationship between incident and reflected angles, and 60° is double the given angle, which violates the law.

hi.stem: यदि आपतन कोण 30° है, तो परावर्तन कोण क्या है?
hi.solution: परावर्तन के नियम कहते हैं कि आपतन कोण परावर्तन कोण के बराबर होता है। इसलिए, यदि आपतन कोण 30° है, तो परावर्तन कोण भी 30° होना चाहिए। अन्य विकल्प इस मूलभूत परावर्तन के सिद्धांत के साथ संगत नहीं हैं। 0° और 90° आपतित और परावर्तित कोणों के बीच संबंध के साथ संगत नहीं हैं, और 60° दिए गए कोण का दोगुना है, जो नियम के विरुद्ध है।
hi.critique: The Hindi translation is accurate, maintains the same meaning, and uses appropriate technical terms as per Indian curriculum.

questions.stem: A person is trying to see a candle flame through a bent pipe. What will happen?

questions.stem: In the pinhole camera experiment, why does the image of the candle flame appear upside down on the screen?
choices: Because the light rays are absorbed

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of light reflection?
questions.solution: A mirror showing your face is an example of light reflection. Light from the object (your face) hits the mirror and bounces back into your eyes, allowing you to see the image. A rainbow is an example of dispersion, a shadow is due to light being blocked, and a light bulb glowing is emission of light. Therefore, the correct answer is that a mirror showing your face is an example of reflection.

questions.stem: If a beam of light from the sun enters a glass of water, what happens to the light?

questions.stem: What happens when light falls on opaque objects?
questions.solution: When light falls on opaque objects, the light is reflected off their surface because opaque materials do not allow light to pass through them. Refraction involves light bending as it passes through a medium, which does not occur with opaque objects. questions.stem: What is the turning back of light rays from the surface of an object called?
questions.solution: The turning back of light rays from the surface of an object is called reflection, which occurs when light bounces off a surface. questions.stem: Why can we see objects around us even if they are not smooth?
choices: Because they reflect light in all directions
questions.solution: The correct answer is that we can see objects around us because they reflect light in all directions. This allows light to reach our eyes from different angles, making the objects visible. Objects do not need to absorb light to be seen, nor do they need to emit light or be transparent to be visible.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the mirrors placed on the moon by astronauts?
choices: To measure the distance between Earth and Moon
To study the properties of light
To create a permanent light source on the moon
questions.solution: The mirrors are used to measure the distance between Earth and the Moon by reflecting laser beams sent from Earth. They are not used for reflecting sunlight, studying light properties, or creating a light source.
